id: title:Gilbert09:accept openssh tunnel keys pasted with extra whitespace

observations.behavior: Re-serializes an OpenSSH-formatted private key into PEM before passing it to Paramiko's parser.
observations.posthog_connection: Warehouse source authentication; this allows users who paste SSH keys with whitespace or formatting changes to authenticate without manual cleanup.

observations.behavior: Removes the seek-to-start call after loading bytes and immediately re-loading from that same object. This could have been redundant if no other reads occurred between these points.
observations.posthog_connection: Minor implementation change in warehouse credential handling; removing unnecessary state reset does not independently establish broader benefit.

observations.behavior: Adds parameterized tests covering four variations of pasted SSH key input: generated, leading whitespace, indented lines, and joined line breaks.
observations.posthog_connection: These checks demonstrate that the fix handles edge cases where a user copies an OpenSSH key and its formatting is altered, supporting reliability claims.

observations.limitations: The tier depends on whether the removal of `file_obj.seek(0)` was intentional or accidental. The hunk P1.F1.H1 removes a line while P1.F1.H2 adds surrounding serialization logic; it's unclear if both hunks are part of one coherent behavior or two separate edits. No test failure before/after is shown to prove regression prevention. No adoption or incident data exists.

review.limitations: The tier depends on whether the removal of `file_obj.seek(0)` was intentional or accidental. The hunk P1.F1.H1 removes a line while P1.F1.H2 adds surrounding serialization logic; it's unclear if both hunks are part of one coherent behavior or two separate edits. No test failure before/after is shown to prove regression prevention. No adoption or incident data exists.
review.reason: Substantive bounded improvement: the code explicitly re-serializes keys with different whitespace/formatting and includes comprehensive parametrized tests showing acceptance of those variants. This demonstrates a correctness/reliability improvement rather than narrow maintenance. However, no systemic risk reduction across multiple components or critical paths is demonstrated, so 3 is not warranted. The removed seek call does not independently establish broader benefit.
review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse source authentication; warehouse users who paste SSH private keys into PostHog can now authenticate even when their copy has leading spaces, indentation, or missing newlines.
review.uncertainty: Whether removing file_obj.seek(0) changes runtime behavior or is incidental; this could shift score toward 1 if that removal had unintended consequences. Grouping issue: P1.F1 contains both an unrelated deletion and an addition; without clearer separation, tier assignment relies on the added serialization and its tests.
